english.title: Recipient of/person obtaining HMRC information disclose information relating to person's identity
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being

(A)_[the recipient of]_
(B)_[a person who had obtained]_

HMRC information from a registrar of companies for England and Wales, without authorisation from HMRC, disclosed information, namely **(..SPECIFY INFORMATION..), which related to a person whose identity

(C)_[was specified in]_
(D)_[could be deduced from]_

the disclosure
english.legislation: Contrary to section 110G(4), (5), (7) of the Companies Act 2006 and section 19(4) of the Commissioners for Revenue and Customs Act 2005.

english.notes:
(i) It is a defence under subsection 1110G(6) for a person charged with this offence to prove that the person reasonably believed that the disclosure was lawful, or that the information had already lawfully been made available to the public.(ii) A prosecution for an offence under this section may be instituted in England and Wales only by or with the consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions, see section 19(5) of the Commissioners for Revenue and Customs Act 2005.
(iii) Civil financial penalties may be issued by the registrar as an alternative to prosecution for this offence, being a ‘relevant offence’ as defined by section 1132A of the Companies Act 2006.
(iv) Civil financial penalties may be issued by the registrar for this offence being a ‘relevant offence’ as defined by section 1132A of the Companies Act 2006. No criminal proceedings may be commenced against a person in respect of conduct amounting to an offence if the person has already been given a financial penalty by the registrar. Further, no financial penalty may be imposed on a person in relation to conduct amounting to an offence if proceedings in respect of that offence are ongoing or the person has been convicted.
